subject: Provisional SLA commitment request: QuantumSearch preview
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Holmes <sara.holmes@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Provisional SLA commitment request: QuantumSearch preview

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the productive demo yesterday. Per our conversation, Acme is planning to run the QuantumSearch preview against a production search workload next week and has asked whether we can provide a provisional SLA for uptime and latency during the preview window.

High level ask from Acme: a provisional uptime commitment and a latency target for p95 on their main search path for the 30-day preview. They understand this is a preview and are open to a temporary carve-out, but want clarity on fallback behavior and what credits/operational guards are in place.

Proposed Redwood approach (initial):
- Provisional uptime: 99.5% for the preview window (30 days)
- Provisional latency target: p95 <= 450ms for the configured search route (US region)
- Automated fallback: when model latency > 700ms or error rate exceeds threshold, traffic automatically reroutes to the stable search model (no SLA)
- Monitoring: access to a dedicated dashboard and 5-minute alerting to Acme ops; weekly latency digest
- Credits: prorated service credit for SLA misses during the preview (to be defined in addendum)

I'm attaching a draft_sla_addendum.pdf and a latency_baseline.csv from our canary run. Monica/Karthik/Marcus — can you confirm feasibility of the latency target and the fallback mechanics? If engineering can confirm the guardrails we can share a formal addendum and a DocuSign link.

Sara — can you confirm the start date you expect for the preview and any procurement constraints (term, PO, required docs)?

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: draft_sla_addendum.pdf (draft), latency_baseline.csv (canary sample)

From: Sara Holmes <sara.holmes@acme.com>

Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 10:40:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Provisional SLA commitment request: QuantumSearch preview

Rachel —

Appreciate the quick follow-up. We want to move fast but I need clarity on a few items before I can greenlight the preview from procurement:
- Duration: we prefer a 30-day pilot but with an option to extend by another 30 days if results look good.
- SLA level: our ideal is 99.9% and p95 <= 350ms. I understand preview constraints; is there a path to 99.9% for the core search route?
- Credits/penalties: please share the proposed credit formula for misses.
- Compliance: procurement also requires SOC2 attestation and a short list of security controls (data retention, logs access) before signing.

I can route an initial PO for the preview if legal/procurement sign off on the addendum. Attaching a procurement_terms.docx with our normal clause set for pilots.

If you can share a confirmed technical baseline from your canary runs and a clearer fallback policy, procurement will likely accept a provisional 99.5% as long as there's a strong rollback/fallback plan and clear credits.

Thanks,
Sara Holmes
Head of Search Engineering | Acme Corp
sara.holmes@acme.com

Looping internal ops/eng to confirm:

Quick summary of questions for engineering before we send the addendum to Acme:
1) Is p95 <= 450ms realistic for the US search route with the preview model given Acme's expected QPS? (We have their projected QPS in the CRM record.)
2) What spikes have you seen in canary runs (long-context queries)? Any mitigation (prompt truncation, shorter context) needed?
3) Can we expose the alerting dashboard to Acme with 5-minute polling and a webhook to their PagerDuty?
4) How intrusive is the fallback to the stable model? Is it a full traffic reroute or per-request failover?

Karthik — tagging you for technical confirmation and to attach any latency graphs. Marcus — will want an approve/deny on the provisional credit approach once engineering confirms the risk.

—Monica
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Provisional SLA commitment request: QuantumSearch preview

Monica — technical notes from canary and recommendations: 
- Canary environment (us-west, A100 pool) observed baseline p95 ~320ms with batching tuned to match Acme's expected request shape. Typical median ~120ms.
- Edge cases: long-context queries (tokens > 1,200) experience p95 spikes up to ~700ms; those are infrequent but visible in the histogram.
- Failure modes: KV-cache cold-start and GPU memory thrash during simultaneous large batches cause most latency spikes.

Recommendations for preview SLA: 
- Accept provisional p95 <= 500ms (US) and provisional uptime 99.5% for 30 days. 500ms gives margin for long-context noise while still meeting a strong UX bar.
- Implement per-request failover: if in-flight latency estimate exceeds threshold or returns an error, route that single request to stable model. This avoids full cluster reroute and reduces blast radius.
- Enable prefix caching for their top 100 queries to reduce tail latency; we can pre-warm during onboarding.
- Expose a read-only monitoring dashboard and webhook for critical alerts.

Attached a canary snapshot (canary_latency_snapshot.png) and I can drop the raw timeseries to the CRM record. If Acme still pushes for 350ms p95, we should discuss a phased plan: start at 500ms for 30 days, then optimize to 350ms post-preview with a committed engineering project (costed separately).

—Karthik
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Attachments: canary_latency_snapshot.png

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sara Holmes <sara.holmes@acme.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Provisional SLA commitment request: QuantumSearch preview

Thanks team — and hi Sara.

After reviewing Karthik's canary data and Monica's notes, Redwood is prepared to offer a provisional SLA for the 30-day QuantumSearch preview under the following conditions:
1) Provisional uptime: 99.5% for the preview window; provisional p95 latency target: <= 500ms (US search route).
2) Automatic per-request failover to the stable model on per-request error or when estimated in-flight latency exceeds configured thresholds.
3) Monitoring: read-only dashboard access and a webhook to Acme PagerDuty, weekly digests.
4) Trial duration: 30 days with an option to extend for a second 30-day period pending a post-trial review.
5) Credit: prorated service credit for SLA misses (detailed in the attached draft addendum).
6) Compliance: Redwood will provide SOC2 Type II report and security control summary prior to start.

This is a provisional, time-limited commitment for the preview only and does not change standard production SLAs. We will memorialize the above in an addendum and route for signature via DocuSign.

Rachel — please send the finalized addendum and DocuSign link and schedule the kickoff for next Tuesday. Sara — if these conditions work for Acme, we can move to signatures.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

- Prewarm: Karthik to pre-warm the prefix cache 24 hours prior to start

Sara, please let me know whether Tue 4/6 10:00am PT works and if procurement needs any edits to the addendum. We'll also provide SOC2 Type II and the security control summary immediately.

Best,
Rachel
